item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russia is intensifying airstrikes on Ukrainian energy sites, including power plants in Kyiv and civilian areas in Zaporizhzhia, while Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries and hit a Russian Iskander-M missile maintenance base. Ukraine also reported hitting six Russian Su-34 bomber jets with a Neptune missile and accused SpaceX of throttling Starlink terminals used for drone operations. Russian authorities detained a Japanese journalist on espionage charges and announced a diesel deal framed as an energy ceasefire, which Ukraine rejected as false. 75,767 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Iraq’s Supreme Court declared the Kurdistan Region security law unconstitutional and US firms are assessing air-defence investment in the Kurdistan Region. item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:

Bandits carried out a separate assault in Borgu LGA, while a Christian humanitarian worker was slain in northwest Nigeria and a Niger lawyer was jailed for a social-media post about the army. The United States added Nigeria to its blacklist for recruiting child soldiers, and Mali expanded its reserve force by 2,400 recruits, including 800 women. These incidents show a widening of violence beyond isolated attacks on security forces to include civilian targets and legal repression.
